title: Global View - Understanding a Trial

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we have a very dramatic intermediate level lesson for you.
segments.zh: 我叫凯瑟琳，今天我们为大家准备了一节非常戏剧化的中级课程。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we're going to take a look at how a court works, for example in the United States.
segments.zh: 今天我们将看看法院的运作方式，例如在美国。

segments.en: So you see that in movies and TV shows a lot, you know, the judge and all that.
segments.zh: 所以你在电影和电视节目中经常看到这一点，你知道，法官等等。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Many of you have seen the movie The Firm or 12 Angry Men.
segments.zh: 你们中许多人都看过电影《The Firm》或《十二怒汉》。

segments.en: These are classics in courtroom dramas we say.
segments.zh: 这些是我们所说的法庭剧中的经典之作。

segments.en: So today we're in a courtroom and there are many characters who are trying to determine if this person is innocent or guilty.
segments.zh: 所以今天我们在法庭上，有许多角色试图确定这个人是无辜的还是有罪的。

segments.en: So let's take a listen and find out what's going on.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听一听，看看发生了什么。

segments.en: Your Honor, ladies and gentlemen of the jury, my client Robert Malone has been accused of a crime he did not commit.
segments.zh: 法官大人，陪审团的女士们，先生们，我的委托人罗伯特·马龙被指控犯有他没有犯下的罪行。

segments.en: The prosecution has accused my client of being a pickpocket.
segments.zh: 检方指控我的当事人扒窃。

segments.en: I know we have heard the testimony of many people here today.
segments.zh: 我知道我们今天在这里听到了许多人的证词。

segments.en: People who claim the defendant, my client, stole their wallets.
segments.zh: 这些人声称，被告，也就是我的当事人，偷了他们的钱包。

segments.en: I feel sorry for these victims.
segments.zh: 我为这些受害者感到难过。

segments.en: I really do.
segments.zh: 我真心这么觉得。

segments.en: But my client is innocent.
segments.zh: 但我的当事人是无辜的。

segments.en: Let's look at the facts.
segments.zh: 让我们看看事实。

segments.en: Number one, these so-called witnesses did not actually see the defendant steal anything.
segments.zh: 第一，这些所谓的证人实际上并没有看到被告偷了任何东西。

segments.en: Number two, when the police stopped him, he did not have any of the stolen wallets.
segments.zh: 第二，当警察拦住他时，他没有任何被盗的钱包。

segments.en: There is no evidence.
segments.zh: 没有证据。

segments.en: Therefore, ladies and gentlemen of the jury, I ask you to think carefully before giving your verdict.
segments.zh: 因此，陪审团的女士们，先生们，我要求你们在做出判决之前仔细考虑。

segments.en: Look at the facts.
segments.zh: 看看事实吧。

segments.en: Look at the evidence.
segments.zh: 看看证据吧。

segments.en: My client is innocent.
segments.zh: 我的当事人是无辜的。

segments.en: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, have you reached a verdict?
segments.zh: 陪审团的女士们，先生们，你们做出了判决吗？

segments.en: Yes, Your Honor.
segments.zh: 是的，法官大人。

segments.en: Our verdict is not guilty.
segments.zh: 我们的判决无罪。

segments.en: Thank you so much.
segments.zh: 非常感谢。

segments.en: You were great.
segments.zh: 你表现得很棒。

segments.en: Thank you for all your hard work.
segments.zh: 感谢您的辛勤工作。

segments.en: You're welcome, Robert.
segments.zh: 不客气，罗伯特。

segments.en: I knew you were innocent, so my job was easy.
segments.zh: 我知道你是无辜的，所以我的工作很轻松。

segments.en: Take care of yourself, okay?
segments.zh: 照顾好自己，好吗？

segments.en: Thanks once again.
segments.zh: 再次感谢。

segments.en: Hey, where's my wallet?
segments.zh: 哎，我的钱包呢？

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So you probably heard a lot of technical words that are specifically related to the courtroom, to lawyers, and the laws.
segments.zh: 所以你可能听到了很多与法庭、律师和法律特别相关的技术词。

segments.en: So why don't we take a look at some of those now in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不看看现在语言要点中的一些。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: The first Language Takeaway we're looking at today is all about people.
segments.zh: 我们今天要看的第一个语言要点是关于人的。

segments.en: So people you will find in a courtroom.
segments.zh: 也就是你在法庭上会遇到的人。

segments.en: Who's the first person on our list, Marco?
segments.zh: 谁是我们名单上的第一个人，马可？

segments.en: So the top person would be the judge.
segments.zh: 所以最重要的人是法官。

segments.en: Now you didn't really see this word judge in the dialogue, right?
segments.zh: 其实你在对话里并没有真正看到 judge 这个词，对吧？

segments.en: You did hear though the phrase, Your Honor.
segments.zh: 你确实听到了这句话，法官大人。

segments.en: Your Honor.
segments.zh: 法官大人。

segments.en: So Your Honor.
segments.zh: 所以法官大人。

segments.en: So that's how you talk to a judge.
segments.zh: 所以这就是你与法官交谈的方式。

segments.en: You always add Your Honor before it or something like that?
segments.zh: 你是总要在前面加上 Your Honor（法官大人）之类的称呼吗？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you know we say Mr. President when we're talking to Barack Obama.
segments.zh: 所以你知道我们在与巴拉克奥巴马交谈时说总统先生。

segments.en: But if we're talking to a judge, he's a special person in American society.
segments.zh: 但如果我们与法官交谈，他是美国社会中的一个特殊人物。

segments.en: So we call him or her Your Honor.
segments.zh: 所以我们称他或她为 Your Honor（法官大人）。

segments.en: Your Honor.
segments.zh: 法官大人。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we have the judge.
segments.zh: 所以我们有法官。

segments.en: That's our first person.
segments.zh: 那是我们的第一个人。

segments.en: Who else do we have?
segments.zh: 我们还有谁？

segments.en: So we have the judge and now we have a group of 12 people who will ultimately decide if the person is guilty or not.
segments.zh: 所以我们有法官，现在我们有一组 12 人，他们最终将决定这个人是否有罪。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So these people are normal.
segments.zh: 所以这些人是正常的。

segments.en: They come from all different parts of society and they will decide what to do with this person.
segments.zh: 他们来自社会的各个不同部分，他们将决定如何处理这个人。

segments.en: Is he guilty or is she innocent?
segments.zh: 他是有罪还是她是无辜的？

segments.en: This group is called the jury.
segments.zh: 这个小组被称为陪审团。

segments.en: So the jury is a group of normal citizens who will listen to both sides of the story and will then decide if the person committed the crime or didn't commit the crime.
segments.zh: 所以陪审团是一群普通公民，他们会听故事的双方，然后决定这个人是犯罪还是没有犯罪。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: A jury.
segments.zh: 陪审团。

segments.en: And the big question is, who's fighting?
segments.zh: 关键问题是，谁在打这场官司？

segments.en: We have two sides.
segments.zh: 我们有两个方面。

segments.en: Someone who is upset and someone who is defending themselves.
segments.zh: 一方是受了委屈的人，一方是为自己辩护的人。

segments.en: The person who is upset, this is the prosecution.
segments.zh: 那个受了委屈的人，就是检方。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So the prosecution has a group of lawyers that are called the prosecutors, right?
segments.zh: 所以检方有一群被称为检察官的律师，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And they're trying to prove that that person committed the crime.
segments.zh: 他们正试图证明那个人犯了罪。

segments.en: For example, I say that Marco burned down my house.
segments.zh: 例如，我说马可烧毁了我的房子。

segments.en: I go to court, I say I am the prosecution.
segments.zh: 我上法庭，我说我是检方。

segments.en: I want him to pay me for my house.
segments.zh: 我要他付钱给我的房子。

segments.en: So I'm the prosecution.
segments.zh: 所以我是控方（检方）。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you're trying to not only prove that I committed the crime, but also trying to get me to pay for the damage that I caused.
segments.zh: 所以你不仅试图证明我犯了罪，还试图让我为我造成的损害付出代价。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So in this case, the prosecution says, this man stole my wallet.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，检方说，这个人偷了我的钱包。

segments.en: He's a pickpocket.
segments.zh: 他是个扒手。

segments.en: And who's the pickpocket?
segments.zh: 谁是扒手？

segments.en: Or maybe the pickpocket.
segments.zh: 或者也许是扒手。

segments.en: Who's the other side of this?
segments.zh: 谁是这方面的另一面？

segments.en: The defendant.
segments.zh: 被告人。

segments.en: Defend, defendant.
segments.zh: 辩护，被告。

segments.en: Think about the word here.
segments.zh: 想想这里的词。

segments.en: To defend is to stand up for yourself, to protect yourself.
segments.zh: defend 就是为自己挺身而出、保护自己。

segments.en: So the defendant says, listen, no, that's not true.
segments.zh: 所以被告说，听着，不，这不是真的。

segments.en: I am not a pickpocket.
segments.zh: 我不是扒手。

segments.en: I didn't do that.
segments.zh: 我没有那样做。

segments.en: So we have the prosecution and the defense.
segments.zh: 所以我们有起诉和辩护。

segments.en: And the person who might be guilty, the person who did the thing or didn't do the thing, is called the defendant.
segments.zh: 可能有罪的人，做这件事或没有做这件事的人被称为被告。

segments.en: So in your example again about the crime that maybe I burnt your house down or I didn't, I would be the defendant and my lawyers would constitute my defense.
segments.zh: 所以在你的例子中，我可能会烧毁你的房子，或者我没有，我将成为被告，我的律师将构成我的辩护。

segments.en: Yeah, they are your defense.
segments.zh: 是的，他们就是你的辩方。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So very technical words, but the important thing to remember here is defendant.
segments.zh: 所以非常技术性的词，但这里要记住的重要一点是被告。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So now we have one key element that is also a person.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们有一个关键元素也是一个人。

segments.en: We have the witness.
segments.zh: 我们有证人。

segments.en: All right, so the basic idea like you said is we have to tell a story.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以像你说的基本想法是我们必须讲故事。

segments.en: My story is that you burned down my house.
segments.zh: 我的故事是你烧毁了我的房子。

segments.en: And you say, no, I didn't.
segments.zh: 你说，不，我没有。

segments.en: Prove it.
segments.zh: 证明给我看。

segments.en: I say, I can.
segments.zh: 我说，我可以。

segments.en: Someone saw you with a lighter.
segments.zh: 有人用打火机看到了你。

segments.en: So this person is my witness.
segments.zh: 所以这个人就是我的证人。

segments.en: That means that he or she saw what happened.
segments.zh: 这意味着他或她看到了发生的事情。

segments.en: So someone who sees a crime is a witness to that crime.
segments.zh: 所以看到犯罪的人，就是那起犯罪的证人。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So a lot of people are in the courtroom.
segments.zh: 所以很多人都在法庭上。

segments.en: A lot of things are happening.
segments.zh: 很多事情正在发生。

segments.en: So I think we should listen to the dialogue again and we'll be back to look at some more words on Language Takeaway Part 2.
segments.zh: 所以我认为我们应该再听一次对话，我们会回来看更多关于语言要点第 2 部分的单词。

segments.en: Your Honor, ladies and gentlemen of the jury, my client Robert Malone has been accused of a crime he did not commit.
segments.zh: 法官大人，陪审团的女士们，先生们，我的委托人罗伯特·马龙被指控犯有他没有犯下的罪行。

segments.en: The prosecution has accused my client of being a pickpocket.
segments.zh: 检方指控我的当事人扒窃。

segments.en: I know we have heard the testimony of many people here today.
segments.zh: 我知道我们今天在这里听到了许多人的证词。

segments.en: People who claim the defendant, my client, stole their wallets.
segments.zh: 这些人声称，被告，也就是我的当事人，偷了他们的钱包。

segments.en: I feel sorry for these victims.
segments.zh: 我为这些受害者感到难过。

segments.en: I really do.
segments.zh: 我真心这么觉得。

segments.en: But my client is innocent.
segments.zh: 但我的当事人是无辜的。

segments.en: Let's look at the facts.
segments.zh: 让我们看看事实。

segments.en: Number one, these so-called witnesses did not actually see the defendant steal anything.
segments.zh: 第一，这些所谓的证人实际上并没有看到被告偷了任何东西。

segments.en: Number two, when the police stopped him, he did not have any of the stolen wallets.
segments.zh: 第二，当警察拦住他时，他没有任何被盗的钱包。

segments.en: There is no evidence.
segments.zh: 没有证据。

segments.en: Therefore, ladies and gentlemen of the jury, I ask you to think carefully before giving your verdict.
segments.zh: 因此，陪审团的女士们，先生们，我要求你们在做出判决之前仔细考虑。

segments.en: Look at the facts.
segments.zh: 看看事实吧。

segments.en: Look at the evidence.
segments.zh: 看看证据吧。

segments.en: My client is innocent.
segments.zh: 我的当事人是无辜的。

segments.en: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, have you reached a verdict?
segments.zh: 陪审团的女士们，先生们，你们做出了判决吗？

segments.en: Yes, Your Honor.
segments.zh: 是的，法官大人。

segments.en: Our verdict is not guilty.
segments.zh: 我们的判决无罪。

segments.en: Thank you so much.
segments.zh: 非常感谢。

segments.en: You were great.
segments.zh: 你表现得很棒。

segments.en: Thank you for all your hard work.
segments.zh: 感谢您的辛勤工作。

segments.en: You're welcome, Robert.
segments.zh: 不客气，罗伯特。

segments.en: I knew you were innocent, so my job was easy.
segments.zh: 我知道你是无辜的，所以我的工作很轻松。

segments.en: Take care of yourself, okay?
segments.zh: 照顾好自己，好吗？

segments.en: Thanks once again.
segments.zh: 再次感谢。

segments.en: Hey, where's my wallet?
segments.zh: 哎，我的钱包呢？

segments.en: I love it when we do this.
segments.zh: 我很喜欢我们一起做这个。

segments.en: So many words.
segments.zh: 这么多单词。

segments.en: So much language to take away.
segments.zh: 有这么多语言知识可以收获。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So now we're going to take a look at the second part of language takeaway where we have another set of four words that we want to take a look at.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们要看看语言要点的第二部分，我们有另一组四个单词，我们想看看。

segments.en: Language takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: The first is actually two words.
segments.zh: 第一个实际上是两个词。

segments.en: We have two opposites.
segments.zh: 我们有两个意思相反的词。

segments.en: Okay?
segments.zh: 好吗?

segments.en: So you said earlier, the jury has to make a decision.
segments.zh: 所以你之前说过，陪审团必须做出决定。

segments.en: The jury has to decide, is the defendant innocent or guilty?
segments.zh: 陪审团必须决定，被告是无辜的还是有罪的？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: These are two important adjectives.
segments.zh: 这是两个重要的形容词。

segments.en: Innocent.
segments.zh: 无辜的。

segments.en: What does this mean?
segments.zh: 这是什么意思？

segments.en: So if he is innocent, that means he did not commit the crime.
segments.zh: 所以如果他是无辜的，那就意味着他没有犯罪。

segments.en: He is not responsible for what happened.
segments.zh: 他不对发生的事情负责。

segments.en: He did not steal the wallets.
segments.zh: 他没有偷钱包。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we often say babies are so innocent.
segments.zh: 所以我们经常说婴儿是如此无辜。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: They can't do anything.
segments.zh: 他们什么都做不了。

segments.en: They can't do anything wrong.
segments.zh: 他们不能做错任何事。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So guilty would be the opposite.
segments.zh: 那 guilty（有罪）就是它的反义词。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So usually when someone is guilty, they're sad, they feel bad, you want them to pay you.
segments.zh: 所以通常当一个人有罪时，他会难过、良心不安，你会希望他赔偿你。

segments.en: And they go to jail.
segments.zh: 他们进了监狱。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: In bad situations, they go to jail.
segments.zh: 在糟糕的情况下，他们会进监狱。

segments.en: If you burn down my house, of course you're going to go to jail.
segments.zh: 如果你烧毁了我的房子，你当然会进监狱。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So guilty means you did a crime.
segments.zh: 所以有罪意味着你犯罪。

segments.en: You did a bad thing.
segments.zh: 你做了一件坏事。

segments.en: So we talked about the prosecution and the defense of the defendant.
segments.zh: 所以我们谈到了控方和被告的辩方。

segments.en: And what happens is they also present some key elements that will prove if the person is innocent or guilty.
segments.zh: 接下来，双方还会出示一些关键要素，用来证明这个人是有罪还是无辜。

segments.en: And those elements are called evidence.
segments.zh: 这些要素就叫作证据。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So back to this idea, we tell a story.
segments.zh: 所以回到刚才那个思路，我们要讲一个故事。

segments.en: Maybe a witness can help us tell our story.
segments.zh: 也许证人可以帮助我们讲述我们的故事。

segments.en: But as you say, evidence is stuff.
segments.zh: 但正如你所说，证据就是东西。

segments.en: It's things.
segments.zh: 是东西。

segments.en: So in the case of the house, I could say you have matches and you smell like smoke and oil.
segments.zh: 所以拿房子这件事来说，我可以说你有火柴，身上还有烟味和油味。

segments.en: This is evidence for me to use to show that you are guilty.
segments.zh: 这是我用来证明你有罪的证据。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So in this case, do we have any evidence?
segments.zh: 那么在这种情况下，我们有任何证据吗？

segments.en: There's no evidence, says the defendant.
segments.zh: 被告说，没有证据。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So evidence is proof.
segments.zh: 所以 evidence 就是 proof（证据）。

segments.en: It's physical proof.
segments.zh: 它是实实在在的证明。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And most of the times when you see movies or TV shows, they will find, I don't know, like maybe a fingerprint that's evidence or somebody's glasses.
segments.zh: 大多数时候，你看电影或电视节目时，他们会发现一些东西，比如一枚作为证据的指纹，或者某人的眼镜。

segments.en: A cell phone.
segments.zh: 一部手机。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So evidence.
segments.zh: 所以证据。

segments.en: This is very important when you want to build a case.
segments.zh: 当你想建立起一个案子时，这非常重要。

segments.en: Finally, at the end of a trial, we have a verdict.
segments.zh: 最后，在审判结束时，我们有一个判决。

segments.en: Now, what is a verdict?
segments.zh: 现在，什么是判决？

segments.en: Well a verdict is a final decision or a conclusion in which the jury says, yeah, the person is guilty or he's not guilty, he's innocent.
segments.zh: 判决是陪审团说的最终决定或结论，是的，这个人有罪或他无罪，他是无辜的。

segments.en: So we use this word usually to reach a verdict.
segments.zh: 所以我们通常使用这个词来做出判决。

segments.en: The jury reaches a verdict.
segments.zh: 陪审团作出判决。

segments.en: Now it's interesting why we say to reach because a jury is not just one person.
segments.zh: 有意思的是，我们为什么用 reach 这个说法，因为陪审团不只有一个人。

segments.en: A jury is many people.
segments.zh: 陪审团很多人。

segments.en: And so these people have to decide together.
segments.zh: 所以这些人必须一起决定。

segments.en: They have to argue.
segments.zh: 他们不得不争论。

segments.en: They have to make a conclusion that everyone agrees on.
segments.zh: 他们必须做出每个人都同意的结论。

segments.en: And this is to reach a conclusion, to reach a verdict because they have to travel there.
segments.zh: 这就是 reach a conclusion、reach a verdict 的意思，因为他们必须一起走到那一步。

segments.en: They have to go together and figure it out.
segments.zh: 他们必须一起去弄清楚。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's very, very important.
segments.zh: 这是非常非常重要的。

segments.en: So the jury reaches a verdict.
segments.zh: 于是陪审团作出判决。

segments.en: And we did have one other phrase that's very interesting.
segments.zh: 我们确实有另一句非常有趣的短语。

segments.en: It doesn't quite fit with the other ones.
segments.zh: 它跟前面几个不太一样。

segments.en: We heard this phrase from the defendant.
segments.zh: 我们从被告那里听到了这句话。

segments.en: The lawyer says, so these so-called witnesses didn't actually see anything.
segments.zh: 律师说，所以这些所谓的证人实际上并没有看到任何东西。

segments.en: What is so-called?
segments.zh: so-called 是什么意思？

segments.en: So he's being sarcastic when he uses this phrase, so-called, right?
segments.zh: 所以当他使用这个所谓的短语时，他是在讽刺，对吧？

segments.en: That's why even his tone changes, these so-called witnesses.
segments.zh: 所以他连语气都变了——“这些所谓的证人”。

segments.en: So it's a way of expressing sarcasm.
segments.zh: 所以这是表达讽刺的一种方式。

segments.en: He's saying they say they're witnesses, but they're not really because they didn't see anything.
segments.zh: 他的意思是，他们自称是证人，但其实不算，因为他们什么也没看到。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So so-called means you say that they are, but they're not really.
segments.zh: 所以所谓的意思是你说他们是，但他们不是真的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I could also say, your so-called lawyer thinks he can help you, but he can't.
segments.zh: 我也可以说：你所谓的律师觉得他能帮你，其实帮不了。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That means I don't think your lawyer is very good.
segments.zh: 这意味着我不认为你的律师很好。

segments.en: I don't think he's a real lawyer.
segments.zh: 我不认为他是一个真正的律师。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Or sometimes people say, my so-called friend stood me up last night.
segments.zh: 或者有时人们会说：我那个所谓的朋友昨晚放了我鸽子。

segments.en: Oh, so it's not really a friend.
segments.zh: 哦，所以他其实不算真正的朋友。

segments.en: He's not really a friend.
segments.zh: 他不是真正的朋友。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So-called.
segments.zh: 所谓的。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: That's another good one.
segments.zh: 这又是一个很好的例子。

segments.en: Let's listen to this dialogue one more time.
segments.zh: 让我们再听一次这次对话。

segments.en: Really think about some of the words you heard today, and we'll be back in a moment.
segments.zh: 好好想想今天听到的一些单词，我们一会儿就回来。

segments.en: Your Honor, ladies and gentlemen of the jury.
segments.zh: 法官大人，陪审团的女士们、先生们。

segments.en: My client, Robert Malone, has been accused of a crime he did not commit.
segments.zh: 我的客户罗伯特·马龙被指控犯有他没有犯下的罪行。

segments.en: The prosecution has accused my client of being a pickpocket.
segments.zh: 检方指控我的当事人扒窃。

segments.en: I know we have heard the testimony of many people here today.
segments.zh: 我知道我们今天在这里听到了许多人的证词。

segments.en: People who claim the defendant, my client, stole their wallets.
segments.zh: 这些人声称，被告，也就是我的当事人，偷了他们的钱包。

segments.en: I feel sorry for these victims.
segments.zh: 我为这些受害者感到难过。

segments.en: I really do.
segments.zh: 我真心这么觉得。

segments.en: But my client is innocent.
segments.zh: 但我的当事人是无辜的。

segments.en: Let's look at the facts.
segments.zh: 让我们看看事实。

segments.en: Number one, these so-called witnesses did not actually see the defendant steal anything.
segments.zh: 第一，这些所谓的证人实际上并没有看到被告偷了任何东西。

segments.en: Number two, when the police stopped him, he did not have any of the stolen wallets.
segments.zh: 第二，当警察拦住他时，他没有任何被盗的钱包。

segments.en: There is no evidence.
segments.zh: 没有证据。

segments.en: Therefore, ladies and gentlemen of the jury, I ask you to think carefully before giving your verdict.
segments.zh: 因此，陪审团的女士们，先生们，我要求你们在做出判决之前仔细考虑。

segments.en: Look at the facts.
segments.zh: 看看事实吧。

segments.en: Look at the evidence.
segments.zh: 看看证据吧。

segments.en: My client is innocent.
segments.zh: 我的当事人是无辜的。

segments.en: Ladies and gentlemen of the jury, have you reached a verdict?
segments.zh: 陪审团的女士们，先生们，你们做出了判决吗？

segments.en: Yes, Your Honor.
segments.zh: 是的，法官大人。

segments.en: Our verdict is not guilty.
segments.zh: 我们的判决无罪。

segments.en: Thank you so much.
segments.zh: 非常感谢。

segments.en: You were great.
segments.zh: 你表现得很棒。

segments.en: Thank you for all your hard work.
segments.zh: 感谢您的辛勤工作。

segments.en: You're welcome, Robert.
segments.zh: 不客气，罗伯特。

segments.en: I knew you were innocent, so my job was easy.
segments.zh: 我知道你是无辜的，所以我的工作很轻松。

segments.en: Take care of yourself, okay?
segments.zh: 照顾好自己，好吗？

segments.en: Thanks once again.
segments.zh: 再次感谢。

segments.en: Hey, where's my wallet?
segments.zh: 哎，我的钱包呢？

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now a very interesting situation with the courtroom dramas.
segments.zh: 所以现在说到法庭剧，有个非常有意思的情况。

segments.en: And I've heard that all the people in the jury have to agree in order for them to reach a verdict, right?
segments.zh: 我听说陪审团中的所有人都必须同意才能做出判决，对吧？

segments.en: So if one of them is not convinced that the person is, for example, guilty, then they have to keep on deliberating.
segments.zh: 所以如果其中一个人不认为这个人有罪，比如说，那他们就得继续商议。

segments.en: That's the word, right?
segments.zh: 这就是这个词，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So basically, the jury is always alone in a room.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，陪审团总是独自待在一个房间里。

segments.en: Maybe they have a guard, but they're not supposed to talk to journalists or friends of the defendant or anyone because their decision is supposed to be pure.
segments.zh: 也许他们有个警卫，但他们不能跟记者、被告的朋友或任何人交谈，因为他们的决定应当不受影响。

segments.en: So they talk, and sometimes it takes 10 minutes.
segments.zh: 所以他们说话，有时需要 10 分钟。

segments.en: Everyone agrees this person is guilty or this person is innocent.
segments.zh: 每个人都同意此人有罪或此人是无辜的。

segments.en: But sometimes they don't agree.
segments.zh: 但有时他们不同意。

segments.en: And it can be one day, two days, a week, two weeks, a month trying to decide what to do.
segments.zh: 可能是一天、两天、一周、两周，甚至一个月，都在商量该怎么办。

segments.en: I remember in the OJ Simpson case, the jury took a long time to figure out what they were going to do.
segments.zh: 我记得在 OJ Simpson 案中，陪审团花了很长时间才弄清楚他们要做什么。

segments.en: And now we said that the jury are common citizens.
segments.zh: 现在我们说陪审团是普通公民。

segments.en: They're normal people.
segments.zh: 他们是普通人。

segments.en: So what happens in their jobs if they can't go to work because they're doing this?
segments.zh: 那么，如果他们因为这样做而不能去上班，他们的工作会发生什么？

segments.en: Well, in America, this job is called jury duty.
segments.zh: 在美国，这件事叫 jury duty（担任陪审员的义务）。

segments.en: And so someone will send you a letter, and they say, listen, you need to come do jury duty and you help be a part of the jury.
segments.zh: 所以会有人给你寄一封信，说：你需要来履行陪审员义务，帮忙成为陪审团的一员。

segments.en: And your job, they can't make you come because this is a service for the government.
segments.zh: 至于你的工作，他们不能强迫你来，因为这是为政府提供的服务。

segments.en: So it's above everything else.
segments.zh: 所以它高于一切。

segments.en: It's above.
segments.zh: 它是优先的。

segments.en: You get your normal pay.
segments.zh: 你照常拿工资。

segments.en: There's no problem.
segments.zh: 没有问题。

segments.en: But it just don't work.
segments.zh: 但它只是不起作用。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So they can't fire you if you're in jury duty for like five days or a month or whatever.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您在陪审团中担任五天或一个月或其他任何事情，他们就不能解雇您。

segments.en: No, they can't.
segments.zh: 不，他们不能。

segments.en: That's illegal.
segments.zh: 那是非法的。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: That's really interesting.
segments.zh: 这真的很有趣。

segments.en: But a lot of people I've heard don't like to go to jury duty for some reason.
segments.zh: 但我听说过的很多人出于某种原因不喜欢去陪审团。

segments.en: Is it tedious?
segments.zh: 它乏味吗?

segments.en: No, it's probably very boring.
segments.zh: 不，这可能很无聊。

segments.en: I've never done it, but it's probably very boring.
segments.zh: 我从来没有做过，但它可能很无聊。

segments.en: I would imagine so.
segments.zh: 我会这样想。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Well, that's a very interesting topic.
segments.zh: 嗯，这是一个非常有趣的话题。

segments.en: I'm sure in your countries, laws are handled differently.
segments.zh: 我敢肯定，在你们国家，法律的处理方式不同。

segments.en: Maybe you don't have a courtroom.
segments.zh: 也许你没有法庭。

segments.en: Maybe you have like in England, people wear wigs.
segments.zh: 也许你们那儿像英国一样，人们要戴假发。

segments.en: And black robes.
segments.zh: 和黑色长袍。

segments.en: So let us know how it works in your countries.
segments.zh: 所以跟我们说说，在你们国家是怎么运作的。

segments.en: We'll see everyone at our website EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 我们会在网站 EnglishPod.com 上和大家见面。

segments.en: And of course, if you have any questions or comments, you can leave those there as well.
segments.zh: 当然，如果您有任何问题或意见，您也可以将其留在那里。

segments.en: See you on the website and happy studies.
segments.zh: 在网站和快乐研究中见。

segments.en: Bye everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。
